title: A repeating 30-year renewal cycle raises mean water age by at most 8.20 percent when mean renewal time is 30 years
abstract: We test how intermittent winter outcrops affect mean age at a fixed mean renewal rate. For a well-mixed box with nonnegative periodic renewal hazard, period T and mean rate 1/tau, we prove the sharp bound tau <= cycle-mean age <= (T/2)coth[T/(2 tau)]. For T=30 years and tau=30 years, intermittency can add at most 2.459 years (8.20 percent). Applied to published 1985-2014 annual outcrop shapes in 40 CMIP6 runs, the 30 runs with positive cumulative area at or above density 26.5 give a median increase of 0.175 years and a maximum of 1.964 years. Each shape is normalized to the same mean rate. The six runs with closed mean maps but open winters give ages of 30.323-31.964 years. Exact interval integration, random hazard checks and separate ODE calculations verify the implementation. These are conditional periodic-box results, not ocean-age estimates. A finite 30-year record retains 36.79 percent of an initial-age difference at tau=30, so the same upper bound does not apply without periodic closure.

display.caption: Sharp periodic renewal-age bound and tests using published annual outcrop shapes. All numerical ages assume a common mean renewal time; they are not actual ocean ages.
